In the buggy version, `initialize()` only calls `__Ownable_init_unchained()`, so the contract remains uninitialized (the `initializer` modifier does not set `_initializing` properly) and `owner()` returns `address(0)` instead of the deployer.

The second version breaks because the missing __Ownable_init_unchained() call causes the contract to not have an owner, but the assertion checks that after calling initialize(), c.owner() returns the deployer address (msg.sender). In the reference version, __Ownable_init_unchained() transfers ownership to msg.sender, so c.owner() == address(this). In the modified version, __Ownable_init_unchained() is not called, so _owner remains address(0), and c.owner() returns address(0), which is not equal to address(this). Thus assertEq(c.owner(), address(this)) passes on reference and fails on modified.
